To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the galaxy cluster Abell 2744, which contains a powerful radio halo, is in a merging phase, as suggested by a variety of statistical analyses of galaxy velocity data.

A2744 is a merging cluster in a late merging phase, that the merging is occuring in a roughly NS direction with a velocity of $\sim 3000~\mbox{km~s}^{-1}\;$and that the radio halo emission is located in the merging region.
A2744 is a dynamically active cluster with an ongoing merging event, which is probably the origin of its diffuse radio halo.

the dynamics of the cluster and the possible connection with the radio halo.

A2744 is a merging system in which a major substructure has been detected in the velocity space, and the cluster radio halo is likely related to the merger process.

the merging scenario is a viable and promising explanation of the complex dynamics of the cluster A2744.

the dynamical properties of A2744 are in good agreement with the presence of an active radio halo.
the cluster A2744 is in a highly disturbed dynamical state, with two clumps in the final phase of merging.

the dynamical state of the galaxy cluster is crucial to understand the physical origin of diffuse radio emission.
the dynamical analysis of galaxy clusters is a crucial tool to unveil the nature of the diffuse radio emission and to constrain the cluster merger history.
the cluster A2744 is a complex object, with a very peculiar dynamical structure and a powerful extended radio emission.
